sections.heading: Starting IB home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Starting is mostly a matter of being specific. IB home tuition in Mumbai is quickest to arrange when the first message contains the subject list with levels written out, the examination session the student is sitting, the next three deadlines with dates on them, and two time windows a week that your household can actually protect. A request that reads only as Maths help in Bandra West takes three more messages before anybody can do anything useful with it.

The first session is a diagnostic and should look like one. Expect the tutor to ask for the last report card, a recent piece of marked work and the current IA draft if one exists, and to spend more of the hour listening and setting questions than explaining. By the end you should have a written statement of where marks are being lost and what the next four sessions will cover. If the first session was all teaching and no diagnosis, say so that evening rather than at the end of the month.

Set the room up once and stop renegotiating it weekly. A table, a chair at the right height, a plug point, the textbook and the calculator kept in the same place, and the television off. In a gated society, send the tutor's name and phone number to the gate as a standing weekly entry instead of raising a visitor pass every time; in older South Mumbai buildings with no lift attendant after 8pm, pick an earlier slot and stop fighting the building. An adult at home for the first two sessions is sensible, in the next room rather than in the room.

Then leave it alone for a month. Weekly interrogation of a teenager about whether the tutor is any good produces very little information and a good deal of friction; marked work and a four-week review produce both. If the subject list is long, stage it: begin with the two subjects where the next deadline falls, add the third once the rhythm holds. Hiring all of them in one week is how families end up with six sessions nobody has the hours to prepare for.
bullets: Subject list with levels written out, and the examination session
The next three deadlines with dates, not approximate months
Two weekly time windows your household can genuinely protect
Last report card, one marked script and any current IA draft
Standing gate entry for the tutor instead of a weekly visitor pass

faqs.question: Is there really such a thing as the best IB tutor, or does it depend on the subject?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on the subject. The phrase best IB tutor in Mumbai describes a match, and the thing being matched is a specific skill: proof reachability in Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL, uncertainty handling in Physics HL, command-term discipline in Biology, an examiner's ear in Language B, historiography in History. A tutor can be outstanding at one of those and ordinary at the rest, which is normal rather than a failing. The practical consequence is that a parent with four weak subjects is hiring two or three people, not one, and should budget attention accordingly.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on five things and none of them is a fixed rate card. Board and level come first, because IGCSE Core work and Diploma Programme HL work are not the same job. Subject scarcity comes next, since Physics HL, Language B and History IA supervision have thinner pools than MYP Mathematics. Travel distance and time of day come third: a 7pm slot in Kharghar costs a tutor more of their evening than the same slot in Khar West. Session length and frequency are fourth, and the fifth is whether the work is contact teaching or read-and-respond supervision.

faqs.question: Can one home tutor cover all my child's IB subjects?
faqs.answer: Usually not well, and it is worth knowing why before you ask. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai is realistic up to about MYP3, where the content is broad and shallow and the thing being taught is study habit. From MYP4 and certainly in the Diploma Programme the subjects diverge: the marking criteria differ, the Internal Assessments differ, and what an examiner rewards differs. One tutor covering Mathematics and Physics is common and sensible. One tutor covering Mathematics, Physics, Economics and English A is a compromise you will feel by the second term.

faqs.question: How do I find good IB tutors near me in Mumbai without relying on word of mouth?
faqs.answer: Start from the subject and level rather than the postcode, then filter by distance. Word of mouth travels by building and by school here, which means you mostly hear about the tutor a neighbour's child had for a different subject at a different level. Searching for IB tutors near me in Mumbai and then asking the subject-specific questions set out above filters much harder than a recommendation does. If the strongest match for a scarce subject sits three zones away, take them online rather than taking a nearer person who does not know the course.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Andheri West for a weekday evening slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the slot is a standing weekly one and the tutor is matched from the same corridor. Andheri West sits on the Western Line and Metro Line 1, so a tutor coming from Santacruz, Khar West or Jogeshwari arrives predictably, while one coming from Chembur across the SCLR at 7pm does not. The workable rule is that a tutor should live or work within about half an hour of your address off-peak, because off-peak half an hour becomes fifty minutes in the evening and that is the version you will get on a Tuesday.

faqs.question: How does society gate access and the visitor pass work for a home tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a standing weekly visitor instead of clearing them at the gate every week. Most Mumbai societies accept a resident's written request naming the tutor, their phone number and the fixed day and time, and some issue a card for it. Share the tower and flat number, the lift the tutor should use and the name the guard will recognise. Sessions that begin fifteen minutes late almost always begin late at the gate rather than at your door, and this fixes most of that.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring actually work for Physics and Chemistry HL?
faqs.answer: For theory and past-paper technique yes, for practical work and the early stages of the Internal Assessment much less so. A tutor on a call can mark a Paper 2 answer, correct an uncertainty calculation and talk a student through a mechanism step by step. What they cannot do is watch how the student sets up a measurement, or catch a graph being sketched wrongly while it happens. The arrangement that holds is hybrid: in person for the practical and diagram-heavy weeks, online for marking and revision, which also survives the monsoon.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. What should I do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the specific diagnosis first, before changing anything else. A month is four or five sessions, which is enough to identify where the marks are going and not enough to move a grade. If the tutor can name the error pattern and show you marked work, give it another month and watch whether that pattern changes. If the answer comes back general, that the basics are weak or that she needs more practice, you have a tutor who has not diagnosed anything, and a replacement beats buying more hours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor supervise the Extended Essay and TOK, or is that only the school's job?
faqs.answer: The school supervises formally and a tutor can support the work around it, and keeping that distinction clear protects the student. The school assigns the Extended Essay supervisor, holds the reflection sessions and submits the work. A tutor helps narrow the research question, reads drafts faster than a school timetable allows, and pushes on the reflections most students leave until the end. For Theory of Knowledge the useful help is turning a prescribed title into real knowledge questions. A tutor who offers to write any part of either is a tutor to decline.

faqs.question: How much does Ghodbunder Road or Peddar Road traffic affect an evening slot?
faqs.answer: Enough that it should decide the slot time rather than be discovered after the slot is booked. On Ghodbunder Road a tutor travelling from Thane station to Kasarvadavali takes twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at 7pm. Peddar Road and Haji Ali back up in much the same way, which is why South Mumbai tutors are matched inside the island. The practical fixes are a 5pm or 8.30pm start instead of 7pm, a weekend morning for the longer session, and an agreed online fallback for the worst evenings.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is simply not the right fit?
faqs.answer: Tell us in one or two specifics and a different tutor for the same subject and level is introduced. Fit failures are usually not competence failures: a precise, quiet tutor and a student who needs pushing can both be good and still not work together, and nobody has to be at fault for the arrangement to end. You do not need to justify the request or sit through a recovery plan. The one timing caution is to avoid switching inside the four weeks before mocks or final examinations, when continuity beats fit.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE Core or Extended the right choice, and who should advise on it?
faqs.answer: Extended unless there is a clear reason otherwise, and the advice should start with the subject teacher. The Core and Extended split caps the grade available in Mathematics and some sciences, so choosing Core for comfort in Year 10 can quietly close a Diploma Programme Higher Level door in Year 12. A tutor's job at that point is to say honestly whether the gap is closeable in the time left. The school knows the student's working pattern; the tutor knows what the Extended paper actually demands of them.

You will get a shortlist of subject specialists with their backgrounds rather than a single name. Pick one, run the first session as a diagnostic at home or online, and ask for the written statement of where marks are being lost before you commit to a full term.

sections.heading: How a Request for the Best IB Gram Home Tuition in Mumbai Becomes a Shortlist
paragraphs: A request for the best IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai arrives as a sentence and has to be turned into something checkable. The intake asks for four things that actually narrow the field: the board and syllabus code your child sits, the year group and level, the specific thing going wrong, and the two or three windows in the week when a tutor could realistically be at your door. Everything else is preference. A parent who writes DP1 Chemistry Higher Level, struggling with energetics, Tuesday and Thursday after seven, Khar West has already done most of the matching work without knowing it.

What happens next is subtraction, not ranking. The pool is filtered by syllabus first, because a tutor fluent in Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 is not automatically fluent in Diploma Programme (DP) Chemistry, and the International Baccalaureate (IB) Internal Assessment (IA) criteria have no Cambridge equivalent. Then by level, because Higher Level (HL) option topics sit outside the Standard Level (SL) course entirely. Then by geography, because a tutor who needs ninety minutes on the Western Express Highway each way will start cancelling by week six. What survives is usually two or three names, and the honest framing is that these are the people who fit the constraints.

Each shortlisted profile comes with the syllabus the tutor has taught, the levels they have taken students through, and the slots they can hold for a full term. You then run your own test, because you know things the form never captured: whether your daughter shuts down when someone talks for ten minutes straight, whether your son needs the physics before the maths or the maths before the physics. The platform narrows; the family decides. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and will not tell you a tutor is the answer to a problem nobody has diagnosed yet.
bullets: 1. Tell us the board, syllabus code, year group and exact level.
2. Name the problem precisely: a unit, a paper, a criterion, a deadline.
3. Give two or three weekly windows plus your pin code or society name.
4. Receive a shortlist of two or three tutors who clear all three filters.
5. Run a first session, then say yes, no, or try the next name.

sections.heading: Which Programme Are You Actually Buying For: IB, IGCSE, or Both?
paragraphs: Usually both, at different ages, and that is precisely why a single ranked list of tutors is useless. The International Baccalaureate runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) to Year 5 or 6, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through middle school, and the Diploma Programme in the final two years. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel run IGCSE across Years 9 and 10, with Core and Extended tiers in several subjects. A Mumbai family with two children often has one in MYP4 and one in DP2, which is two completely different tutoring problems sharing one dining table.

IB Gram's brief covers all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE, Years 1-12 with a home tutor in Mumbai, but nobody should read that as one person doing all of it. PYP and early MYP work rewards a tutor who can teach around inquiry units and keep a child reading. MYP4 and MYP5 reward one who knows the criteria-based marking that bewilders parents raised on percentages. DP is a different trade again: two years, six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and an Internal Assessment in every single subject.

IGCSE sits in the middle and carries its own decision. Core or Extended in Mathematics, the choice between Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607, whether to take a language at first or second language level: these are Year 9 decisions that set the ceiling for DP two years later. A tutor who has only taught DP will give you a confident answer about Extended Mathematics and be wrong about the paper structure. Asking for all IB and IGCSE subjects with one tutor in Mumbai is asking for a generalist at the exact moment the decision in front of you needs a specialist.

sections.heading: Does Best Mean the Same Thing in HL Physics and IGCSE Core Maths?
paragraphs: No, and the gap is wider than most parents expect. Higher Level Physics asks a tutor to handle the option topic, the data-based question in Paper 3, and an Internal Assessment where the marks sit in the analysis and evaluation criteria rather than in the practical itself. IGCSE Core Mathematics asks for something close to the opposite: patient, high-volume practice on a restricted syllabus where the grade ceiling is fixed and the win is clean arithmetic under time pressure. One tutor can do both. Most do one of them properly.

Subject choice across both boards, HL/SL and Core/Extended decisions, and the internal assessments each one carries are where a match either works or quietly fails. Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL and Mathematics Applications and Interpretations SL share a name and little else: the Applications IA rewards a real data set and a defensible modelling decision, the Analysis IA rewards a mathematical idea pushed further than the syllabus goes. English Language and Literature HL carries the Individual Oral and the HL Essay. Business Management, Economics and Psychology each have their own IA shape, word limit and command terms.

Take a DP2 student at a Juhu school sitting May exams. Her Chemistry IA draft is due in the same fortnight as her TOK essay and her Economics commentary. She does not need the finest chemist in the city; she needs someone who can read a draft against the five IA criteria, say which one is costing her marks, and get her to a submittable version in three sessions without writing it for her. By March that same student needs paper technique and timing instead. Hiring for February and keeping through March is how families get both, and it is a visibly different brief each month.

sections.heading: What Does Best Available Mean in Each of Mumbai's Six Zones?
paragraphs: It means something different in each, because supply is not spread evenly across Mumbai, Maharashtra. South Mumbai holds deep IGCSE and DP experience concentrated in a small area: tutors working around Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road and Fort are almost always matched inside the island, because a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening. The Coastal Road has eased the north-south run; the Harbour Line and the Churchgate end of the Western Line carry the rest.

The Western Suburbs hold the largest pool, strung along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway from Bandra West and Khar West through Santacruz, Juhu and Andheri West up to Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar. Matching along the line works; matching across it does not. Metro Lines 2A and 7 have made Dahisar to Andheri viable on a weekday evening in a way the Link Road never was. The Central Suburbs run on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR. Powai is the exception: physically central, no station of its own, reached by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Kurla or Ghatkopar.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road and the Eastern Freeway, which puts South Mumbai within reach of Chembur and Wadala faster than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is nodal: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, linked by Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, with the Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line shortening the island run. Tutors there are matched node to node. Thane spreads from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, and Ghodbunder sets the timetable: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour at seven. The Bandra-Worli Sea Link and Metro Line 3 matter for island crossings, Metro Line 1 for the Versova to Ghatkopar run.
bullets: South Mumbai: deep DP and IGCSE supply, short distances, slow evenings
Western Suburbs: largest pool; match along the Western Line, not across it

sections.heading: The Mumbai School Calendar Decides When a Good Match Matters Most
paragraphs: Mumbai's IB and IGCSE schools run a June-to-April year, and the pressure points are predictable enough to hire against. Families at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, the Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School at Cuffe Parade and Bombay International School at Babulnath sit broadly the same deadlines, because the deadlines come from the board rather than the school. August and September are quiet. October to December is when DP1 subject choices become irreversible and MYP5 students begin IGCSE coursework in earnest.

January and February are the hardest fortnights of the year in this city. DP2 Internal Assessment deadlines cluster, the Extended Essay goes final, mocks land, and a tutor who was comfortable with one session a week is suddenly asked for three. This is when the available pool shrinks most, and it is the strongest single argument for hiring in November instead of January. Students at Oberoi International School on JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, JBCN International School in Chembur, NES International School in Mulund West and Thakur International School in Kandivali East are all inside that same squeeze.

March to May is exam season for the May session, and October to November for the November session, which a smaller number of Mumbai schools use. IGCSE candidates sit in May and June or in October and November depending on their cohort. Families at Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane, D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Singapore International School in Dahisar East and Billabong High International School in Santacruz plan around the same windows. sections.heading: Home Tuition, Online or Hybrid: Which Is Best for Your Child in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition wins for most Mumbai families below Year 11, online wins for scarce Higher Level subjects, and hybrid is what actually survives a full term. Parents who search for the best IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai almost always mean a tutor at the dining table, and there is a solid reason for that: a child driven to a class at eight in the evening on the Western Express Highway loses the session twice over, once in the car going and once coming back. IB home tuition in Mumbai moves the commute off the child and onto the adult who is paid for it.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves the problem home tuition cannot touch: supply. If you need Higher Level Further Mathematics, Design Technology, Film or a less common Language B, the person who has actually marked that syllabus may be in Pune, Bengaluru or Dubai, and insisting on a body in the room means settling for someone who has never taught it. Online works well for a DP2 student annotating an IA draft on a shared screen, and badly for a Year 7 who needs someone to notice she stopped writing four minutes ago. An IB private tutor Mumbai families book online should still be asked how they handle a student who goes quiet.

Hybrid is the arrangement most families land on by December without having planned it. One session at home each week for the work that needs supervision, one online for the draft review or the problem-set walkthrough, and the online slot absorbs the monsoon evening when Ghodbunder Road or the Sion-Panvel Highway is standing still. Treat the online option as the thing that keeps a term intact rather than as a downgrade. The real question is not which mode is better in general; it is which mode your child's attention and your family's week can hold through February.

sections.heading: The Five Dimensions a Mumbai Home Tutor Match Is Actually Judged On
paragraphs: A match, not a person, is what succeeds or fails, and it is judged on five things. Board and syllabus fluency: has this tutor taught the exact syllabus, not a cousin of it. Level depth: can they go a layer past the syllabus when a bright Higher Level student asks why. Diagnostic ability: in the first session, can they find the real gap instead of starting at chapter one. Logistics that hold for a term: a slot and a route that still work in February, not only in August. Fit with this particular student: pace, tolerance for silence, and whether they teach by question or by explanation.

IB Gram checks the first two and the fourth before a profile reaches you. Claimed syllabus experience is matched against what the tutor says they have taught and the levels they have taken students through, identity is confirmed, and the slot is confirmed against the travel they are agreeing to rather than the travel they hope for. The third and fifth cannot be read off a profile by anyone, including us. An IB home tutor in Mumbai who looks strongest on paper is sometimes the one who talks for fifty minutes while a quiet child nods along. That is the entire reason the first session exists.

Ask for the syllabus code and the last year the tutor taught it. Ask what the command terms in your child's subject are and listen for whether the answer is specific or decorative. Ask what they would do in the first twenty minutes, and be sceptical of anyone who says they would start from the beginning of the course. For an IGCSE student, ask which paper they think is costing marks and why. The best IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai is simply whatever survives that conversation, which is a lower and far more useful bar than a ranking.

sections.heading: How to Define Your Own Best Before You Look at a Single Profile
paragraphs: Tutor rankings do not survive contact with a real request. The variables that decide the outcome are the board, the level, the subject, the student's personality, the week's genuinely spare hours and the distance to your door, and no ordering of names can hold all six at once. Typing IB tutors near me in Mumbai into Google returns a list sorted mostly by advertising budget. Any platform telling you it supplies the best tutors in Mumbai is making a claim it cannot support: it has not met your child, read the IA draft, or tested whether a tutor from Vashi will still be crossing to Chembur in February. We are not going to make that claim either.

So write your own definition of the best IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai before you look at anybody. Four lines is enough: the board and syllabus code, the level, the one thing that must be different in six weeks, and the two windows in the week that are honestly free. The third line is the one families skip and the one that decides everything. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai cannot be judged against, because the request says nothing. A tutor who can take a DP2 Economics commentary from a weak draft to a submittable one before the February deadline can be judged, accepted or rejected inside three sessions.

Then test the shortlist against your four lines rather than against a label. Give each candidate the same twenty-minute problem: here is the draft, here is the mock paper, here is where she got stuck. Watch whether they ask to see the work before proposing a plan. Count how much of the first session they spend talking. Ask what they would drop if only four weeks remained, because a tutor who will not prioritise under a deadline has misread the brief. Two candidates who both look excellent will answer that question differently, and one of those two answers will fit your child.

sections.heading: What Progress Looks Like at Four Weeks, One Term and One Exam Cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see process, not marks. Homework comes back annotated, your child can say what a criterion actually asks for, and the panic about one topic has moved to a different topic, which is progress even when it does not feel like any. Marks lag by design: an IB school reports on internal assessments set weeks apart, so a genuine improvement in understanding in October often surfaces only in a December report. Anyone promising a visible grade change inside a month is selling something. We do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor in Mumbai will.

At one term, expect a measurable change in one or two specific things: a paper the student stops losing time on, an IA criterion that moves from the bottom band to the middle, a Core candidate who is now plausibly an Extended one. At one exam cycle, expect the mock-to-final gap to narrow rather than a transformation. A DP2 student sitting at a four in HL Chemistry in the November mocks and taking May exams has roughly five working months, two of which are consumed by IA and EE deadlines. Honest planning starts from that arithmetic, not from an aspiration.

If it is not working, say so in week three rather than week ten. The usual signals are a tutor who arrives without having looked at last week's work, sessions that drift into general conversation, or a child who is calmer but no clearer. Tell us what specifically is failing and the replacement is drawn from the same shortlist, which is why the shortlist carried more than one name. There is no penalty for changing and no obligation to have the awkward conversation with the tutor yourself. A second match works more often than a second attempt at the first one.

sections.heading: Starting Home Tuition in Mumbai: What to Prepare Before the First Session
paragraphs: Three documents make the first session twice as useful: the most recent report or mock paper with the marks still on it, the subject guide or syllabus code, and whatever the teacher wrote on the last piece of marked work. Add the weekly timetable, because the gap between school finishing at three and sport finishing at six is the real constraint, not your preference. If your building needs a gate pass for a repeat visitor, start that on the day you book rather than on the evening a tutor is standing at the gate in Kharghar or Mulund.

The first session is a diagnosis, not a lesson. Expect the tutor to read the marked work before teaching anything, to ask your child to attempt one question out loud, and to leave with a short plan naming what the next four sessions will cover and in what order. Ask for that plan in writing. If the first session ends with a general promise to build strong foundations and not one named topic, that is your signal to try the next name on the shortlist rather than waiting a month to find out.

What it costs depends on the board and level, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. A Higher Level Physics tutor crossing from Andheri to Chembur twice a week is a different number from an IGCSE Maths tutor two buildings away in Bandra West, and anyone quoting one flat rate for all IB and IGCSE subjects with a home tutor in Mumbai has not asked enough questions yet. Our fees page handles that detail properly. Agree the rate, the session length and the cancellation rule in writing before session one.

faqs.question: Is there such a thing as the best IB tutor in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: No, and the question is worth replacing. The phrase best IB Gram home tuition in Mumbai describes a search, not a specification. There is a strongest match for a particular student, subject, level and week, and that match changes the moment any one of those changes. A tutor who is outstanding on a DP2 Physics Internal Assessment can be a poor choice for a Year 9 deciding between Core and Extended Mathematics. The useful question is narrower: who is strongest for this syllabus, at this level, within reach of our address, in the two hours we actually have free. That version has an answer you can check.

faqs.question: How do I compare two tutors who both look good on paper?
faqs.answer: Give them the same twenty-minute task and watch the difference. Hand each one the same marked paper or IA draft and ask what they would do first. One will ask to see the work and name a criterion; the other will describe a general approach. Then ask what they would drop if only four weeks remained before the deadline. A tutor who refuses to prioritise has not read the situation. Finally, count how much of the session they spent talking against how much they spent listening to your child attempt something. Those three signals separate two identical-looking profiles faster than any list of credentials.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach our building in Thane on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, if the match is made inside Thane rather than across the city. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali on Ghodbunder Road in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so a seven o'clock slot on Ghodbunder is a different commitment from a seven o'clock slot near Majiwada or Pokhran Road. Mulund tutors cross over on the Eastern Express Highway and some hold that well for a term. What does not hold is a tutor brought up from the Western Suburbs for a weekday evening. Weekend slots are a separate conversation.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but somebody should be in the flat. For younger students a parent in the next room is enough and genuinely useful, because you will hear whether the tutor is explaining or lecturing. For DP students, hovering is counterproductive, and most work better with the door open and nobody listening. What matters more than presence is the handover: two minutes at the end where the tutor says what was covered and what the homework is. If you cannot be there, ask for that handover as a message instead, and read it the same evening.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board and level first, then subject scarcity, travel and session length. A Higher Level science or a less common Language B costs more than a widely taught IGCSE subject, because far fewer people have actually taught it. A tutor crossing a zone twice a week prices in the travel, which is one reason a match inside your own node is often cheaper as well as more reliable. Longer sessions usually cost less per hour than short ones. We publish no single rate, because a single rate across subjects would be invented; our fees page explains the variables one at a time.

faqs.question: We live in Navi Mumbai and the tutor is in Bandra. Will that commute hold for a term?
faqs.answer: Probably not for a weekday evening slot. The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have made the crossing faster than it used to be, but a tutor leaving Bandra at six to reach Nerul or Kharghar is committing to a long return on the Sion-Panvel Highway twice a week, and those arrangements usually break in the second month. Match inside Navi Mumbai, node to node along Palm Beach Road, for the standing weekly slots. Keep the cross-creek tutor for a weekend session, or move that one subject online, which is frequently the better trade.

faqs.question: There has been no progress after a month. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for evidence before you ask for a replacement. Request the session log and the last two pieces of marked work, and look at whether the tutor named specific topics or worked in generalities. Often the problem is the brief: a tutor asked to improve Maths will drift, while a tutor asked to fix probability and the Paper 2 time split will not. If the brief was specific and the work still shows no change in approach, that is a mismatch rather than a slow start, and moving to the next name on the shortlist is the right call.

faqs.question: How does replacing a tutor who is not working out actually happen?
faqs.answer: Tell us what is not working and the next name on the original shortlist is contacted. You do not have to manage the conversation with the outgoing tutor, and nothing beyond one line about what went wrong is required, although that line helps us match better the second time. Sessions already taught are paid for and nothing further is owed. The handover works best if you pass on the session log, so the replacement starts from what has already been covered instead of restarting the course from the beginning.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for Higher Level subjects?
faqs.answer: For DP1 and DP2 it works well, and occasionally better than a room. Internal Assessment draft review, problem sets and past-paper walkthroughs are screen-friendly: both people look at the same document and the tutor annotates it live. The honest limits are practical subjects where equipment matters and younger students who need somebody physically present to notice a stall. The stronger argument for online at Higher Level is supply: for a scarce option topic the real choice is an online specialist or a local generalist, and the specialist usually produces the better term.

faqs.question: Which room in the flat works best for home classes?
faqs.answer: The dining table beats a bedroom in most Mumbai flats. It gives a hard surface for papers and a graphing calculator, it is visible, and it signals that this is work rather than company. A bedroom desk suits a DP student who needs two screens and quiet. What does not work is a sofa, a television within earshot, or a room a younger sibling walks through every ten minutes. Sort out the lighting and a power socket for a laptop before the first session and the tutor will not lose fifteen minutes of it hunting for an extension cord.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram affiliated with any of the schools listed on this page?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to any school, board or examination body named here. Those schools appear because their calendars and board pathways shape when a Mumbai family needs help and what kind of help, not because of any relationship. Tutors are matched on the syllabus they have taught, which is often the same syllabus a given school follows, and that is the whole of the connection. We also do not guarantee grades, and anyone in this market who does should be treated with real scepticism.

faqs.question: Do you cover all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes across Mumbai?
faqs.answer: Across the main subjects yes, and for a few rare options the honest answer is online only. Mathematics, the three sciences, Economics, Business Management, Psychology, English, Hindi, French and Spanish have reasonable supply in most zones of Mumbai. Less common Diploma Programme options, second-language choices and some arts subjects are thin even in the Western Suburbs, and in Navi Mumbai or Thane they may not exist locally at all. In those cases we say so plainly and offer an online specialist rather than sending somebody who has never taught the syllabus.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram shortlist a Mumbai home tutor your child will actually talk to?
paragraphs: By asking about your child before asking about the syllabus. Before we shortlist a single name, we want to know what the last teacher your child got on with did differently, and what the last one they switched off from did. Those two answers narrow a list faster than a subject requirement does, because subject competence is common and the rest is not.

Almost every enquiry reaches us from the parent, which is how it should be, because the parent is the one arranging the schedule and paying the bill. But a parent's description of the problem is usually a description of the symptom: the Chemistry grade dropped two points, the Internal Assessment (IA) draft is three weeks late, homework now takes until eleven at night. The student's description of the same situation is almost never about marks. It is about the experience of asking a question. A teacher who sighed. A class that moved on while they were still copying the previous line. A tutor who answered a neater question than the one they had asked, so they stopped asking. Build a shortlist on the parent's version alone and you can place a technically excellent tutor directly into the behaviour the student has already stopped tolerating.

So the sequence is deliberately short. 1. Send the board, the year group, the subjects and your locality, plus the weekday evenings that are genuinely free once school and travel are accounted for. 2. Answer one question about a teacher your child has learned something from, and one about a teacher they gave up on. 3. We shortlist tutors who have taught that board at that level and who can reach your building every week without a two-hour commute at each end. 4. Your child sits the first session, and afterwards you ask one specific question instead of asking how it went.

Step four is the one families skip, and it is the only step that tests the match. We also ask, where the student is old enough to have a view, whether they want a parent within earshot or the door shut. A Year 9 or Year 10 student often says within earshot. A Diploma Programme (DP) student almost always says shut, and a parent who overrides that answer has turned the sessions into something being done to their child rather than with them. Every shortlisted name arrives with the reason it was shortlisted, so you can see whether we matched the subject or the person.

sections.heading: What MYP, DP and IGCSE students in Mumbai each ask for
paragraphs: The programme changes the student's request far more than the subject does. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) student in Khar West and a DP student in Powai can be working through the same mechanics content and want two unrelated things from an IB home tutor in Mumbai. Matching the subject and ignoring the programme is how a competent tutor ends up being described at home as useless.

MYP students complain about criteria more than content. Marks arrive as achievement levels against criteria A to D, with descriptors written in language a thirteen-year-old cannot convert into an action. What they say is that they do not know what the teacher wants. What they need is someone who will put a level 5 response and a level 7 response next to each other and name the difference in one sentence, rather than restating the descriptor more slowly. Primary Years Programme (PYP) parents are usually further back than that: the useful work there is reading, number confidence and the habit of explaining an answer out loud, not exam technique.

IGCSE students want predictability, and the boards give it to them. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both publish past papers and mark schemes, and a Year 10 student's honest request is almost always the same: tell me whether what I just wrote would get the mark. Core and Extended decisions sit underneath that. A student pushed onto Extended Maths because the school expects it, who is quietly drowning in the algebra, will not say so to a tutor who has already told them it is easy. They will say so to one who says the Extended paper is a real step up and here is the gap we are closing.

DP students want to be treated as adults, and the programme agrees with them. They are choosing Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) combinations, carrying an IA in every subject, writing an Extended Essay (EE) and sitting Theory of Knowledge (TOK). A seventeen-year-old who is managing six subjects plus the core has a working view of where their own time is best spent, and it is often more accurate than the parent's. The tutor who asks what they want to use the two hours for, and then holds them to it, gets further than the one who arrives with a fixed plan.

IGCSE: past papers and mark schemes, with an honest read on Core versus Extended
DP: HL and SL load, IA supervision, EE deadlines and TOK sitting on top
PYP: reading, number confidence and explaining an answer out loud
Ask the DP student where the two hours should go before deciding for them

sections.heading: Which subjects do Mumbai students most often say they have given up on?
paragraphs: Maths and Chemistry, and almost never the whole subject. A student who announces that they are bad at Maths will, if you ask one more question, name quadratics in Year 9, or logarithms, or one Paper 2 question that went badly in a mock. The subject did not collapse. A specific fortnight did, and nobody went back for it.

That is why subject choice across both boards matters as much as teaching quality. All IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai is asked to cover carry their own internal assessment, and the assessment is usually where the resistance starts. Maths Analysis and Approaches at HL asks for proof and algebraic fluency that Applications and Interpretation does not; a student who chose AA because a friend did, and who cannot see why the fluency matters, will describe every session as pointless until somebody shows them a Paper 1 question they can now finish. In Chemistry, the structured questions on Paper 2 punish vocabulary rather than understanding, so a student who knows the chemistry and writes it loosely loses marks and concludes they do not know the chemistry.

A worked example from DP1 Physics. A student has finished the data collection for an IA on the extension of a spring and is stuck on the uncertainty column. She asks how to work out the uncertainty on a gradient. A tutor who says that bit is easy, just add the ranges, has lost her, because it was not easy, she had already tried, and now she believes the problem is her. A tutor who says that uncertainties are where most students lose the marks in this criterion, and here is the one method the examiners accept, has kept her, and the method takes the same ten minutes either way. The difference is not knowledge. It is whether the honest answer about difficulty got said out loud.

The same pattern runs through the other subjects students most often ask for. English Language and Literature Paper 1 feels unfair until somebody shows how a guided analysis is actually built. Economics diagrams carry marks that students throw away by drawing fast. Biology command terms decide whether a correct answer scores. IGCSE students taking separate sciences rather than Combined carry three syllabuses and three sets of practical expectations, and that load, not ability, is usually what the giving-up is about.
bullets: Maths: AA versus AI, and whether the algebraic fluency has actually been built
Chemistry and Biology: command terms and vocabulary cost more marks than concepts
Physics IA: uncertainties and gradients, the criterion students quietly abandon
English Paper 1: guided analysis taught as a structure, not as a talent
IGCSE separate sciences: three syllabuses and three practical loads, not one

sections.heading: Mumbai home tuition zone by zone, from Colaba to Kasarvadavali
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six tutoring markets sharing one name, and what the best IB Gram home tutor in Mumbai looks like changes with the zone, because travel decides who can actually hold the same slot every week for a whole term. Students notice this before parents do. A tutor who arrives late and then rushes the last twenty minutes is the single most common complaint we hear from a teenager, and it is almost always a routing problem rather than a character one.

South Mumbai is short in kilometres and slow in minutes. A tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba or Cuffe Parade covers very little ground and can still lose most of an hour to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, so matches here stay on the island: Walkeshwar, Babulnath, Tardeo and Fort tutors cover Walkeshwar, Babulnath, Tardeo and Fort. The Western Line between Churchgate, Grant Road and Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line down to Dockyard and Sewri, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade towards BKC and the Coastal Road all help, but none of them beat matching locally. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Express Highway, the Western Line and Link Road, with Metro Line 1 crossing at Andheri and Metro Lines 2A and 7 running up to Dahisar. Bandra to Khar West to Santacruz is easy along the line; Juhu to Oshiwara to Goregaon East to Malad to Kandivali to Borivali works the same way. Crossing the line at six in the evening does not, and the Bandra-Worli Sea Link only helps the Bandra to Worli direction.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR in between. Powai is the exception worth planning around: it is central on a map and has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar or Kurla, and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road is what makes a Chembur to Powai slot viable at all. The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi through Vikhroli and Bhandup up to Mulund, on the Central and Harbour lines, with the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail from Chembur to Wadala making South Mumbai far closer than it looks.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so we match node to node: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and the Trans-Harbour Line and the Atal Setu have changed the commute without changing the arithmetic of a weekday evening. Pulling a tutor across the creek from the island city for a 7pm slot rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads west to east from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road, and the Ghodbunder stretch sets the timetable: a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening, which is why Thane tutors cover Thane and only Mulund tutors reliably cross over.

Central Suburbs: Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Ghatkopar, Kanjurmarg, reached by JVLR and the SCLR
Eastern Suburbs: Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup, Mulund, Wadala
Navi Mumbai: Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Panvel, matched node to node
Thane: Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Ghodbunder Road, Kasarvadavali

sections.heading: The Mumbai school calendar your teenager is actually living in
paragraphs: The international school year here opens in June and the pressure arrives in predictable blocks, which matters because a student's opinion of a tutor is heavily coloured by which block they are in. Ask a DP2 student in late January whether the tutor is any good and you are asking someone who has an IA deadline, a mock timetable and a TOK essay in the same fortnight. The same student in July will give you a calmer and more accurate answer.

Families across the city deal with much the same rhythm. Students at Dhirubhai Ambani International School and the American School of Bombay in BKC, Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Oberoi International School on JVLR, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, NES International School in Mulund West, the JBCN International School campuses at Parel, Borivali, Oshiwara and Chembur, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all sit against the same assessment calendar even where the boards and campuses differ.

October brings the half-term break and the first set of honest reports. November and December carry MYP summative work and IGCSE mocks for the May and June series. January and February are the worst stretch in the DP year, with internal deadlines stacked against mock exams and predicted grades being formed. March and April are revision months, and the May examination session closes it. A November session exists too, and a handful of students here sit it, which quietly shifts their entire year forward by six months. If you are starting home tuition in Mumbai in January for a DP2 student, say so plainly to the tutor, because triage and teaching are different jobs.

One thing to be clear about: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools named above, with the International Baccalaureate organisation, or with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We name schools because their calendars and board pathways are the local context a tutor has to work inside, not because we represent them or they represent us.

sections.heading: Home classes, online or hybrid: which one does your child prefer and why?
paragraphs: Ask them, because the answer is rarely the one you would guess and it is a real preference rather than a whim. Home tutoring is what most Mumbai families want and what we lead with: a tutor in the room, the student's own notebook open, nothing to log into, and a parent who can see that the session is happening. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student who needs more structure than they are willing to ask for, that physical presence does most of the work on its own.

It also carries costs that students feel more sharply than parents. A tutor travelling to Kandivali or Kasarvadavali on a Tuesday evening is subject to the road, so a late arrival eats the session, and a cancelled session is harder to move than an online one. Home classes also happen in front of the family. More than one student has told us they prefer IB online tutoring in Mumbai purely because nobody in the next room can hear them admit they do not understand simultaneous equations. That is not shyness to be argued out of. It is a condition for honesty, and honesty is the thing that makes the tuition work.

An IB online tutor in Mumbai solves travel and scarcity. If your child needs HL Economics or Higher Level Chinese and the nearest specialist is in another zone, online is the match that exists rather than the match that is ideal. It loses real things: shared paper, the tutor glancing at the working and spotting the error in line three, and the ability to tell at a glance that attention has gone. Younger students fade faster on screen, and a student who does not want the camera on will not be read accurately by anyone.

Hybrid is what most of our longer-running arrangements settle into, and it is worth asking for deliberately rather than drifting into it. One weekly session at home for the teaching and the accountability, one shorter online session for IA questions, past paper marking or the night before a test. If your child tells you the best IB Gram home classes in Mumbai are the ones where the door is shut and the parent is downstairs, believe them and arrange it that way. If they tell you an IB private tutor in Mumbai coming to the flat makes them feel watched, hybrid is how you keep the arrangement without overriding them.

sections.heading: What IB Gram verifies, and what only your child can tell you
paragraphs: Families who search for the best IB Gram home tutor in Mumbai are usually asking a verification question, so here is the short version. We check identity documents, we check that the claimed teaching history for that board and level is real, we check subject claims against what the tutor has actually taught rather than what they studied, and we take references before a tutor is matched. Credentials that cannot be evidenced do not go on a profile.

That process has a hard ceiling, and it is worth naming. Verification tells you a tutor can teach HL Maths. It cannot tell you how they behave in the four minutes after your child gives a wrong answer, and those four minutes decide whether this lasts a term. No document, reference or interview reaches that. Only the student in the room does, which makes your fifteen-year-old the most important part of the checking process and the part most families never consult.

So give them something specific to report on, because a teenager asked for a verdict will give you a verdict and nothing useful. There are four things only they can see. Whether they were allowed to finish a wrong answer before being corrected, or cut off at the third word. Whether the question they asked got answered, or a tidier question got answered instead. Whether they were told a topic is hard when it is hard, or told it was easy and left to conclude the problem was them. And whether anything they said in the session came back to them later in a parent's voice.

There is also a check you should run yourself, separately from us. Watch what happens to the questions your child asks you. A student who is being taught well starts explaining things at dinner without being asked, and corrects you occasionally. A student who has quietly withdrawn stops mentioning the subject at all, and the sessions continue happening on the calendar. The second pattern is the one to act on, and it shows up weeks before a report card does.

sections.heading: What does a student mean by the best IB Gram home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Something much more specific than a parent means. Ask a sixteen-year-old and you do not get qualifications. You get a short list of behaviours, usually five: the tutor does not make them feel stupid for not knowing something, lets them finish a wrong answer, answers the question they actually asked, says plainly when a topic is hard, and does not report every stumble to their parents. That is the student's standard, and a tutor can satisfy every parental criterion while failing all five.

The last of the five is the one that quietly decides everything, and it is worth thinking through properly. A student who believes that whatever they say in the session will be repeated at the dinner table stops saying the useful things. They stop saying they did not understand last week either. They stop saying they have not started the IA. They perform comprehension for two hours a week, which is expensive and useless. The workable line is this: the tutor reports to you on what was covered, what the student can now do that they could not before, what is still weak, attendance, and anything that genuinely worries them about wellbeing or workload. The tutor does not relay every wrong answer, every admission of not having read the chapter, or every grumble about a school teacher. Say that out loud in front of both of them at the start, because a student who hears that boundary being set is a student who will tell the tutor the truth in week one instead of week nine. Parents who have asked us for this have generally found the reporting improves rather than thins out, because what comes back is a diagnosis instead of a transcript.

The other frequent mismatch is age-shaped. A DP student wants to be treated as an adult while a parent is still arranging the schedule, choosing the tutor and sitting in on the first call, and both positions are reasonable. The arrangement that holds gives the student the things that cost nothing: they pick the slot from two or three options, they set the agenda for each session, and they are in the room when the tutor talks about progress rather than being discussed afterwards. Parents keep the money, the hiring and the ending. A Year 9 or Year 10 student is the opposite problem. They need more structure than they want, and they will say they are fine working alone when they are not. There, the honest answer is that the structure is not negotiable but its shape is: they do not get to skip the weekly session, and they do get to choose whether it is Tuesday or Thursday and which subject leads.

One sentence on fees, because it belongs to another page: what you pay turns on board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, and any site quoting you a single number for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai has not asked enough questions. The thing worth paying attention to here is that the cheapest session your child refuses to engage with costs more than the dearer one they look forward to.

sections.heading: Liking a tutor and learning from one are not the same thing
paragraphs: The mismatch runs in both directions and parents usually only check one of them. A student can genuinely enjoy sessions with a tutor who never pushes them: the hour is pleasant, the explanations are clear, nothing is ever difficult, and the marks do not move because the student has never once been stuck in front of them. Equally, a student can dislike a tutor who is doing the job properly, because being corrected is uncomfortable and being asked to redo a question you thought was finished feels like criticism.

The way to tell them apart is not to ask whether they like the tutor. It is to look for unprompted explanation. A student who is learning will, within a few weeks, explain something to you that nobody asked them about, use a phrase they did not have before, or tell you that the school teacher got something slightly wrong. A student in a pleasant arrangement that is going nowhere has no new vocabulary and nothing to say about the subject. That signal is reliable and it is free.

A realistic timeline, in plain terms. At four weeks you should expect two things only: your child can describe what the tutor does in a session, and one specific weakness has been named. Not a grade change. At one term, expect visible change in the mechanical parts of the subject, submitted work that is on time more often than not, and a more accurate sense from the tutor of where the student will land. By one full exam cycle, with consistent attendance and work done between sessions, you should see movement that matches the effort that went in.

What we will not tell you is that a grade is coming. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is guessing with your money. Attendance, the work done between sessions, how late in the year the help started and how much ground was missing all decide the outcome, and only one of those is the tutor's. What we can be accountable for is a tutor who holds the slot, knows the board and level, and tells you the truth about where your child is. If a tutor is not working out, you tell us and we match someone else; your reason stays between you and us, and the student does not have to deliver the news.

sections.heading: Asking your teenager for an honest opinion, and getting one
paragraphs: Start by not asking the question you want to ask. How was it gets fine, every time, from every teenager in the city, because it reads as a request for reassurance and your child is being kind. Specific questions get specific answers. What did you ask him today, and what did he say. Did he let you finish. Was there anything you did not understand and did not mention. Would you rather have him again next week or try someone else.

Timing matters as much as wording. Ask in the car, on a walk, or while something else is happening, not across a table with eye contact and a decision riding on it. Ask once, a day or two after the session rather than in the first ten minutes, and then let it sit. If the answer is lukewarm, do not act on it the same evening; a single session with a new person is a bad sample, and a student who learns that one shrug ends an arrangement will start shrugging strategically. Two sessions in, a lukewarm answer is information worth acting on.

Then listen for the difference between a complaint about the tutor and a complaint about the subject. He goes too fast and he does not explain is about the tutor. I hate Chemistry and it is pointless is usually about three bad weeks in Chemistry and is exactly what a tutor is for. Parents who confuse the two either replace a good tutor or keep a bad one, and both are expensive. If what you hear is that your child feels stupid in the sessions, that is not a subject complaint and it does not improve on its own.

To start, have four things ready: the board and year group, the subjects and whether each is HL, SL, Core or Extended, the last report or mark sheet, and two or three weekday evening slots that are genuinely free. A first session with a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai should spend most of its time diagnosing: what the student can already do, where the gap actually starts, and what the next four weeks will cover. If your child comes out of it able to tell you one thing they understand now that they did not at six o'clock, the match is worth a second week.

faqs.question: My daughter says the tutor is fine, but I do not think she is learning anything. What do I do?
faqs.answer: Stop asking whether she likes him and start looking for unprompted explanation. A student who is learning will, within a few weeks, use a term she did not have before, explain something nobody asked about, or tell you her school teacher got a detail wrong. If none of that is happening, the sessions are probably comfortable rather than useful, which is the most common failure we see and the hardest for a parent to spot. Ask the tutor one direct question: name the weakness you are working on and how I will know when it is fixed. A tutor doing the job can answer that in two sentences.

faqs.question: Should the tutor tell me everything my child says in a session?
faqs.answer: No, and insisting on it will cost you the honesty the tuition depends on. A workable boundary is that the tutor reports what was covered, what your child can now do that they could not before, what is still weak, attendance, and anything genuinely worrying about workload or wellbeing. Not every wrong answer, not every admission of having skipped the reading, not every grumble about a school teacher. A student who believes everything is relayed stops saying what they do not understand, and then you are paying for a performance. Set this out loud in front of both of them at the start, not quietly afterwards.

faqs.question: How do I ask a teenager for an honest opinion about a tutor and actually get one?
faqs.answer: Ask a narrow question at a low-stakes moment and do not act on the answer immediately. What did you ask her today and what did she say beats how was it, because the second one is a request for reassurance and your child will give you one. Ask in the car or on a walk, a day or two after the session, and ask once. Make clear that saying it was not great is not a complaint that gets anyone fired that evening, because a student who thinks one shrug ends an arrangement will either shrug strategically or stay silent out of guilt. Two sessions of lukewarm answers is real information.

faqs.question: My son is in DP2 and says he will arrange his own tutoring. Should I let him?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the split matters. Give him the things that cost nothing and buy cooperation: he picks his slot from the options that work, he sets the agenda for each session, and he sits in when progress is discussed rather than being discussed afterwards. You keep the hiring, the money and the decision to end it. A seventeen-year-old carrying six subjects, an IA in each, the Extended Essay and TOK usually has a sharper read on where two hours should go than anyone else in the house. Overriding that read is the fastest way to turn a good tutor into an appointment he resents.

faqs.question: What does IB Gram actually verify before a tutor reaches my child?
faqs.answer: Identity documents, the claimed teaching history for that specific board and level, subject claims checked against what the tutor has taught rather than what they studied, and references taken before any match. Anything that cannot be evidenced does not appear on a profile. What verification cannot see is behaviour: how a tutor responds in the four minutes after your child gives a wrong answer. Your child is the only person who observes that, which is why we ask you to pass on their view after the first session. Your child's answer decides whether this is the best IB Gram home tutor in Mumbai for them, not ours.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our building in Lower Parel on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the realistic window there is between about half six and half nine on weekdays. Lower Parel and Worli are reachable from South Mumbai and from Chembur and Wadala through the Eastern Freeway, so the pool is reasonable. What breaks a Lower Parel slot is not distance but the Peddar Road and Haji Ali direction in peak hour, so we match from the side of the city the tutor already lives on. Tell us the two evenings that are genuinely free after school and travel, rather than the ones that are theoretically free, and ask for a fixed weekly time instead of a floating one.

faqs.question: Our society in Kharghar requires a gate pass for every visitor. How does that work each week?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once as a recurring visitor rather than clearing them at the gate every week. Most Navi Mumbai complexes in Kharghar, Belapur and Nerul allow a standing entry for a regular service visitor once a resident confirms the name, the day and the slot, usually through the society app or the facility office. Do that in the first fortnight, because repeated gate delays shorten sessions and students notice the rushed ending more than parents do. Also decide where the session will happen: a dining table with the television off works better than a bedroom, and the clubhouse study room works only if it is genuinely quiet.

faqs.question: What do IB tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, level, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, in roughly that order of effect. HL DP subjects cost more than MYP support, a Higher Level subject with few qualified teachers in the city costs more than a common one, and a tutor crossing two zones for a weekday evening slot is pricing in two hours of their own travel. Anybody quoting one number before asking the board and level has not asked enough questions, so we quote after the requirement is clear. One thing worth weighing: a cheaper session your child disengages from costs more per unit of learning than a dearer one they turn up willing to.

faqs.question: There has been no visible progress after a month. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: At four weeks, yes, if two other things are true. Your child should be able to describe what happens in a session, and one specific weakness should have been named by the tutor. If both are true, the work is underway and grades are a slower indicator than parents expect, particularly mid-term where the next data point may be months away. If neither is true after a month, that is a match problem rather than a patience problem, and you should tell us. We do not guarantee grades and will not pretend a month is enough to judge an outcome, but a month is plenty to judge whether a diagnosis has happened.

faqs.question: Does online tutoring work if my child does not like talking on camera?
faqs.answer: It can work better than home tuition for some students, and the camera is worth negotiating rather than enforcing. Several students have told us they prefer online precisely because nobody in the next room hears them admit they are lost, and that privacy is what makes them ask real questions. The trade-off is that the tutor loses the glance at the working that catches an error in line three, so insist on a shared document or photographed working instead. For a Year 9 student, screen attention fades faster, so hybrid usually suits better: one home session weekly and a shorter online one for questions.

faqs.question: My Year 9 child wants fewer rules, not more structure. Who decides?
faqs.answer: You decide that there is structure; they decide its shape. A Year 9 or Year 10 student usually needs more scaffolding than they are willing to ask for, and will tell you confidently that they work better alone when the evidence says otherwise. The version that holds is to make the weekly session non-negotiable while handing over the choices that are genuinely theirs: Tuesday or Thursday, which subject leads, whether a parent sits nearby or not. Giving away the small decisions is what stops the big one being fought every week, and it costs you nothing you actually needed.

faqs.question: The tutor is not working out. How does a replacement happen, and will they be told why?
faqs.answer: Message us and we match someone else; you do not owe the first tutor an explanation and your reason stays between you and us. We will ask what did not work, because it changes the next shortlist, and we will ask specifically whether the issue was teaching, timing or how your child was spoken to. Those lead to different matches. Your child should not be the one delivering the news, and should not be asked to justify the decision to the tutor at the next session. One request we make: give it two sessions before deciding, unless something was said that you would not accept from any teacher.

sections.heading: How a search for the best IGCSE coaching in Mumbai becomes a shortlist
paragraphs: The message that arrives in the second week of January reads the same every year. A Year 11 parent has seen a final-term revision programme advertised, the May series is four months out, and the question is whether to pay for the course or find a tutor instead. Before we answer that, we ask three things: what the mock results actually looked like paper by paper, which tier the student is entered for, and whether the weak spot is content never learned or technique never practised. Those are different problems and they want different money spent on them.

From that message to a shortlist runs in four steps. 1. You tell us the board the subjects and the suburb along with the two or three weekly slots that genuinely exist in your household's week. 2. We filter for tutors who already teach those exact papers at IGCSE and can reach your building inside the travel window you named. 3. You receive a short list with each tutor's subject background teaching history and the standing slot they can hold through to the exam series. 4. You meet one or two of them before committing to anything longer than a single session.

We do not send a name within the hour. A match made on speed in January is a match that breaks in March, usually because the tutor took a slot across the city that was never going to survive the evening peak. It is better to wait two days for a tutor who lives on your side of the Western Express Highway than to start on Monday with one who will be forty minutes late by February.

January matching is also slot-led rather than preference-led. The tutors with free weekday evenings in the final term are the ones who have not already filled their calendar with DP2 and Year 11 students, so the honest sequence is to secure the slot first and refine the subject split afterwards. Families who start this in September choose from a wider pool; families who start in January choose from the pool that is left, which is a real cost of waiting and worth saying plainly. We match across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 with a tutor in Mumbai who teaches the specific paper, so a late request narrows on slots rather than on standards.

sections.heading: What a final-term IGCSE revision programme actually contains
paragraphs: A revision course is not a teaching course and the good ones do not pretend to be. What you are buying is a fixed number of contact hours spent on material the student has already met once: timed papers, mark scheme walkthroughs, worked corrections, and a schedule somebody else designed. The teaching happened over two years at school. The course compresses the review of it. Read any brochure with that distinction in mind and most of them sort themselves into honest and dishonest very quickly.

Tier matters more than parents expect. Cambridge International Education splits most IGCSE subjects into Core and Extended, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses Foundation and Higher in several subjects. A Core candidate sitting in a room where the worked examples are Extended questions spends the weekend watching material that cannot appear on the paper. Ask which tier the course is pitched at before anything else. A programme that answers "both" is telling you the group is mixed and the pace will suit neither end of it.

Families moving towards the International Baccalaureate (IB) have a second decision running underneath the first. Subject choice across both boards feeds forward: Extended Maths and the separate sciences keep Higher Level (HL) options open in the Diploma Programme (DP), while Core Maths closes several of them. An IGCSE revision course will not discuss that, because it is scoped to one exam series. A tutor working with the family across the final term usually does, which is one of the quieter arguments for IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai alongside, or instead of, a course.

The third thing to establish is what is produced at the end. A programme that hands back marked scripts with examiner-style annotation has given the student something to work from in April. A programme that delivers slides and a PDF pack has given them revision material they already had. Ask which one it is, and ask who does the marking, because a course marked by the person who taught it reads very differently from a course marked by nobody.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects respond to short revision and which simply do not
paragraphs: Mathematics is the subject revision courses handle best, because the shortfall is usually fluency rather than ignorance. A student who can do simultaneous equations slowly becomes a student who can do them quickly, and on the calculator paper that is worth real marks. The same course does nothing for a student who never understood indices in Year 9, because every topic above indices then sits on sand. That one distinction decides whether a February programme is money well spent or a month returned empty.

The sciences split along the practical papers. Physics, Chemistry and Biology each carry an alternative-to-practical component, and it is the most coachable paper in the whole IGCSE suite: reading a measuring cylinder to the correct precision, drawing a line of best fit that ignores the anomalous point, writing a control variable as a measurable quantity rather than a vague promise. A weekend on that paper can move a grade boundary. A weekend on the theory papers rarely does, because the theory content is two years deep.

English First Language behaves differently again. The directed writing and the summary question reward a format that can genuinely be taught in a short programme: identify the audience, identify the purpose, lift the right details, compress without copying. The reading response question rewards reading that happened over two years and cannot be installed in four sessions. Business Studies and Economics sit in the middle, where data response technique improves quickly and case study knowledge does not. Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai should be able to tell you which half of each subject is actually in play before the first session is booked.

Second language subjects are the ones most often mis-sold. A student taking French or Spanish at IGCSE who has fallen behind needs vocabulary built over months and spoken practice twice a week, not an intensive weekend. If a revision programme lists eight subjects including two languages on the same timetable, that is a scheduling achievement rather than a teaching one, and it is worth asking how the language hours are staffed.
